content.title: About
content.content: Pretzel chips are crunchy slices of dough formed into small pieces and baked until golden. They contain no added flavors, offering a neutral, slightly salty taste typical of traditional plain pretzels.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The firm texture is achieved by double‑baking at high temperature.
The classic pretzel knot symbolizes infinity, but chips are usually rectangular or triangular.
Pretzel chips are often used as a base for sauces and dips because of their neutral flavor profile.
In the United States they are a popular bar snack, while in Europe they often accompany cheese platters.
One legend says the pretzel shape represents crossed arms of medieval brewers.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Pretzel chips contain virtually no sugar, making them suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: The dough provides slowly released energy.

items.title: Contains small amounts of iron
items.content: Iron is essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain versions add fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Unlike many other snack foods, they are typically baked with little added oil.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Made from wheat flour, pretzel chips can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Even without flavorings, they are often salted; those monitoring sodium intake should limit portions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While less fatty than potato chips, they still provide a notable amount of calories.

items.title: Risk of overeating
items.content: The crunchy texture can lead to rapid consumption of large quantities.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzel chips can be enjoyed straight from the bag, paired with dips (cheese, hummus, guacamole) or added to salads for extra crunch. Their sturdy packaging makes them convenient for on‑the‑go snacking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to maintain crispness. Avoid moisture, which will make them soft.
